title: One-dimensional finite scalar outflow
question: Can the canonical coupled production solver carry a compact scalar pulse out of a finite one-dimensional patch without exciting the incoming scalar characteristic or wrapping into the opposite edge?
prediction: At least 35 percent of the initial scalar energy leaves by time 0.12, the incoming-to-outgoing right-boundary characteristic ratio remains below 1e-8, the opposite-edge amplitude stays below 1e-12, and all registered recovery, constraint, carrier-balance, convexity, and entropy-residual vetoes pass.
falsifier: Insufficient scalar-energy loss, measurable incoming characteristic excitation, opposite-edge contamination, failed recovery or convexity, excessive constraints, carrier imbalance, or an entropy-balance residual above the declared finite-patch tolerance falsifies the passage.
controls: The patch is centered on zero so the existing radial CCZ4 operator has the correct outward orientation on both faces.
The initial Pi=Phi_x pulse is the right-moving scalar characteristic and begins with zero right-boundary incoming field.
The nonperiodic grid shift uses constant edge extrapolation and cannot wrap the upper-face pulse into the lower face.
Scalar, Proca, CCZ4, recovery, convexity, carrier, and entropy diagnostics remain separate vetoes.
The periodic production backend and every previously sealed campaign input remain unchanged.
seed_rationale: The Gaussian pulse, material background, and evolution are deterministic.
